_comment: A bank of standing preferences a developer really says to an assistant.
`sentence` is planted verbatim into a real session as a NEW human turn, so it is
also the quote a correct model must return; `text` is the short canonical form the
memory line would carry. Phrasings are deliberately varied ('always', 'never',
'from now on', 'for future reference', 'stop doing', 'I prefer') because the judge's
job is to recognise a standing preference by its force, not by a trigger word.

preferences.text: Always run the tests before saying a change is done.
preferences.sentence: Always run the full test suite before you tell me a change is done — I don't want to hear "should work" again.

preferences.text: Never force-push to a shared branch.
preferences.sentence: Never force-push to a shared branch. If history needs fixing, open a new branch and tell me.

preferences.text: Use uv, not pip or poetry, for Python dependency work.
preferences.sentence: From now on use uv for anything Python — not pip, not poetry — including running scripts and adding dependencies.

preferences.text: Show the command and its real output rather than describing the result.
preferences.sentence: For future reference, I want to see the actual command and its real output, not a description of what you think it printed.

preferences.text: Do not add emoji to code, commits, or file output.
preferences.sentence: Stop putting emoji in code and commit messages. Plain text only in anything that lands in a file.

preferences.text: Prefer small focused commits over one large one.
preferences.sentence: I prefer small focused commits over one big one — one logical change per commit, even if that means five commits.
Always ask me before you install anything system-wide or change my shell configuration.

preferences.text: Do not write comments that restate the code.
preferences.sentence: Never write a comment that just restates the line below it — comment the why, or write nothing.

preferences.text: Lead with the answer, then the reasoning.
preferences.sentence: From now on, lead with the answer and put the reasoning underneath it. I read the first line and decide whether to keep going.

preferences.text: Do not open a pull request without being asked.
preferences.sentence: Stop opening pull requests on your own. Push the branch, tell me it's ready, and let me decide when a PR goes up.

preferences.text: Use type hints on every new Python function.
preferences.sentence: I prefer every new Python function to carry type hints on its parameters and its return, no exceptions for helpers.

preferences.text: Say when you are unsure rather than guessing.
preferences.sentence: Always tell me when you're unsure instead of guessing confidently — a hedge I can check beats a wrong answer I trust.
